transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park, Priya Menon, Carlos Vega (Redwood) — Maya Chen, Derek Ross, Lena Ortiz, Samir Patel (Peregrine)

Summary section (auto):
Jordan: quick QBR-style checkin to walk through the recent spike, the cost delta, and next steps for a short pilot. Maya: want to validate dedicated runway and autoscale assumptions before peak.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight 45-ish but room for Qs. Jordan Park from Redwood — with Priya our SE and Carlos our CSM. Maya, Derek, you good?
[00:12] Maya: Yep, thanks Jordan. We pulled people in because the traffic spike last week was...unexpected, and our bill jump is, uh, not ideal.
[00:20] Derek: Hey all, quick context: we rolled out version 2 of the conversation model on Tuesday, saw a 3x token volume increase and latency  p95 sorta rose into the 600-700ms territory on the hosted tier.
[00:34] Priya: mhm, the 600-700ms lines up with queueing at the request broker; curious, are you hitting the long tail of sequence lengths more than before?
[00:45] Maya: Yeah we changed prompts, added more context per user — average seq length jumped from ~200 tokens to ~420. Also, we enabled streaming so more small responses but longer prompts.
[00:58] Priya: ok that explains both cost and latency push. Two levers: route heavier requests to Dedicated / pin to a higher-throughput model variant, or shrink context with local caching and prompt engineering.
[01:10] Derek: We'd like to avoid losing quality by prompt changes. What about Dedicated? pricing is the big unknown — the committed pool cost vs per-token hosted.
[01:22] Carlos: right, we can show a line-by-line cost comparison. The big drivers are reserved GPU hours, sustained throughput, and your sequence length profile. I'll share a cost matrix with examples that map to your 3 usage buckets.
[01:36] Samir: also need to ensure we meet SOC2 and SSO requirements. We were told Redwood Private has a VPC option — any gotchas on certs or KMS?
[01:47] Priya: Private has KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SSO via SAML OK. One caveat is on-prem/air-gapped packaging timelines — if you need air-gap, that's a separate engagement. For VPC peering we typically need a maintenance window of an hour for firewall rules and peering setup.
[02:02] Lena: and is audit log retention configurable? We have to keep 1 year for certain flows.
[02:08] Carlos: yes, audit retention is configurable as an add-on — I'll include retention options in the pack.

[02:20] Jordan: let's walk the fast root-cause of the spike. Priya, any immediate guesses?
[02:25] Priya: initial hypothesis: model change => seq length increase => KV cache miss ratio went up. We saw fewer prefix hits so more recompute. Also batching effectiveness drops with long-tail sequences. On Dedicated we can tune continuous batching kernels and optional quantization profiles to get per-token throughput up.
[02:44] Derek: we tried to enable prefix caching last month — maybe mis-configured? The logs show a lot of "KV cash miss" — and sometimes the agent transforms show 'k v cash' so maybe the labeler messed it up in logs.
[02:59] Priya: (laughs) classic transcription. We'll parse logs together — if your prefix key format changed with the new prompt templating, cache keys won't match. Small change but big perf.

[03:12] Maya: ok so immediate actions we'd want: a short bench to simulate 100k tokens/day for 72 hours, confirm P95 under Dedicated, and a cost model for committed monthly vs hosting.
[03:24] Priya: yes, propose 72-hour run on a small Dedicated pool with the same model family (we can use a quantized variant for cost parity) — we'll run with your traffic pattern CSV you mentioned. Priya: we'll collect P50/P95/P99, tail latency, and token throughput.
[03:42] Jordan: timeline wise, we can get that scheduled next week if you provide logs by Friday. Pilot target start the first week of Oct — is that still the plan?
[03:52] Maya: Oct 5-12 window looks good but we need security signoff prior.
[03:58] Carlos: I'll attach the security pack: SOC2 cert, architecture diagram, SAML/SSO walkthrough, KMS notes, and an audit log sample file.

[04:12] Derek: two questions on routing — can we route based on latency SLO or by cost budget? For example, cold path goes to hosted, hot path to Dedicated.
[04:22] Priya: yes, smart routing policies support rules like "route by TTL, latency bucket, or by user tier." You can fallback to a lower-cost variant if Dedicated is saturated. We'll show config examples.
[04:34] Samir: is there rate limiting we can put at token-level per API key? We want to avoid runaway during campaign spikes.
[04:40] Carlos: yes, token-level quotas and per-key throttling exist; we also have alert hooks into your pager if thresholds are exceeded.

[04:52] Jordan: let's capture acceptance criteria for the pilot — what does success look like for Peregrine?
[04:58] Maya: three things: (1) P95 latency under 250ms for 95% of weekday traffic, (2) total monthly token spend no more than 20% over current baseline after expected growth, (3) zero data leakage with audit logs and KMS controls verified.
[05:12] Derek: add: ability to autoscale within the Dedicated pool to handle 3x baseline for 2-hour blasts.
[05:18] Priya: good, we'll map those to bench metrics and autoscale policy parameters.

[05:30] Priya: small technical note — your model is GPT-like architecture with long context; quantization to int8 plus KV cache tuning gives ~1.8x throughput on A100-style instances, but nvcc kernel selection and attention optimizations matter. We'll include recommended instance types and quantization profiles.
[05:50] Derek: hm, can Redwood run those kernel-optimized images in our VPC? We need to ensure the binaries comply with our approved list.
[05:58] Priya: yes, for VPC we ship container images that are validated, but if you require certified binaries we can coordinate. That may take extra security review.

[06:12] Maya: any concerns about model rollout? We do gradual canary, but if a canary hits, what's rollback policy?
[06:20] Carlos: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variant or to hosted fallback. We'll also provide tracing hooks so you can correlate quality regressions.

[06:34] Samir: vendor comparison: we've had conversations with Anthropic and VF — how do you position versus them?
[06:42] Jordan: short answer: we focus on predictable economics and ops controls — routing, caching, and capacity abstractions that keep latency SLOs while reducing per-token spend. Others are strong on model quality or pre-trained safety nets; our differentiation is production-first orchestration.

[06:58] Derek: ok sounds reasonable. Let's talk about cost examples — Carlos, can you walk two scenarios: hosted vs dedicated with our current traffic shape?
[07:06] Carlos: sure: scenario A hosted at current volume would be X per month (we'll fill X in the doc) but with the 3x burst you'd see ~2.7x cost due to increased seq length. Scenario B Dedicated with a 4-GPU reserved pool plus burst capacity yields lower per-token cost after amortization, and with caching we expect a 30-40% cost reduction on steady-state traffic. I'll send the spreadsheet.
[07:29] Maya: will you include sensitivity to seq length in the sheet? That's the thing that changed.
[07:33] Carlos: yes, I've flagged a toggled column for average seq length.

[07:40] Jordan: quick technical checkpoint — Priya, can you confirm what telemetry we need from Peregrine to run accurate sims?
[07:47] Priya: 7-day traffic CSV with timestamps, avg/median/95 seq lengths, payload sizes. Also a sample of prefixed keys to validate cache key schema. And any transformation layers that mutate prompts.
[07:59] Maya: we can export that by Friday.

[08:08] Priya: ok on the bench: we'll run your CSV, 72-hour run, measure P50/P95/P99 and cost. We'll also run a cache-hit experiment toggling prefix formats to show impact.
[08:21] Derek: how much time does the bench need to provision?
[08:26] Priya: a couple hours to provision, then 72 hours to run, then 48 hours to analyze — total ~6 days for full deliverable. If we parallelize analysis we can shorten it.

[08:40] Maya: about SLAs — we need to confirm uptime commitments for Dedicated and escalation paths.
[08:47] Carlos: Dedicated offers SLA-backed uptime with an on-call escalation list; higher support tiers have faster response. I'll include the SLA appendix.

[09:00] Samir: any compliance gaps we should be aware of ahead of the security review?
[09:05] Priya: nothing major; we'll highlight the few items: certified HSM integration timelines and any extra paperwork for data residency. If you need EU-only residency, that's feasible but needs a region commitment.

[09:18] Derek: let's lock dates: Carlos sends cost pack by 9/17, Jordan SOW by 9/18, Priya bench script by 9/20, bench runs 9/21-9/24, analysis by 9/26, pilot planning for Oct 5. Are we aligned?
[09:31] All: yes.

[09:36] Jordan: anything else?
[09:38] Maya: one small ask — can Redwood share example model rollback telemetry? We want to see examples of regressions detected and the rollback sequence.
[09:46] Priya: yes, we'll include a short runbook with examples.

[09:52] Jordan: great — we'll follow up with the docs and action items. Thanks everyone.

[09:58] Derek: thanks.
[10:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional mis-attributions and auto-caption issues present; proper nouns like "KV cache" sometimes appear as "KV cash" or 'k v cash'.
notes: Customer provided initial CSV for traffic patterns, see shared drive link in CRM note (link not exported)
Security pack to include SOC2 report and SAML guide; CSM to attach
questions: What exact SLO thresholds are required for Dedicated SLA?
Are certified HSM binaries required for VPC deployment?
